look_here_first: LOOK FIRST at stem HAI​RS and panicle shape, not dry habitat: Julia's goldenrod has an evenly white-soft-hairy (densely villoso-tomentose) stem, narrow 3-nerved middle leaves often 5–10 mm wide with moderately dense fine hairs, and a LONG NARROW pyramid-like branching panicle about 3–4 times longer than wide. It occurs in Edwards Plateau/Trans-Pecos grassy or open woodland sites AND along WET stream/lake edges. Site moisture alone cannot distinguish it.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: stem continuously soft white tomentose; narrow 3-nerved pubescent leaves 5–10 mm wide; long narrow panicle 3–4 times long as broad; Edwards Plateau and Trans-Pecos population; habitats wet streams, grasslands and woodland

key_traits.label: Comparison training
key_traits.text: Compared with smoother, wetter-site S. gigantea, S. juliae is a drier-site Central/west Texas species with more visibly hairy/canescent foliage.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: FNA: evenly densely villoso-tomentose (fine thin crisped white hairs) along stems 50–250 cm, generally 1–5 stems.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: FNA: narrow lanceolate 3-nerved 50–80(–120) × 5–10(–12) mm, margins shallowly toothed/near entire, both sides moderately to densely hairy.

key_traits.label: Flowering axis
key_traits.text: FNA: narrowly pyramidal panicle approximately 3–4 times as long as wide, 80–950 heads; involucres ~3–4 mm. Compare broad arching panicle giant and tall goldenrods.

key_traits.label: Habitat corrected
key_traits.text: Can occur on wet stream/lake margins AND grasslands or oak/pine woodland, 300–1000+ m; not a dry-site-only species.
